post_saad_rizwan_founder_01.author: SAAD RIZWAN
post_saad_rizwan_founder_01.content:
In an emergency, every second counts. That is why I founded SAFE bd—a national digital safety and emergency response ecosystem designed to bridge the gap between citizens and rapid assistance.

SAFE (Safety • Awareness • Fast Response • Emergency Assistance) brings critical tools right to your fingertips:

Instant SOS: A simple, high-priority emergency button to summon help immediately.

Live Location Sharing: Securely alerts your trusted contacts and authorities when you need it most.

Community Awareness: Structured safety reporting and emergency preparedness tools for a safer society.

We are building a future where trusted help is always within reach. Stay tuned for more updates on our journey!

— Saad Rizwan

Founder, SAFE bd.

post_1792081435440_9363.author: Shabbir
post_1792081435440_9363.content:
I see every day how crime, harassment, and the fear of assault affect our neighbors, families, and particularly women and youth. Safety isn't just the job of law enforcement—it is a collective responsibility. Crime thrives where there is isolation and silence, but it retreats when a community stands together, alert and unified.
We cannot always predict danger, but we can make our neighborhoods hostile to it by taking these four key steps together:
1️⃣ Banish the "Not My Business" Mindset (Active Bystander Intervention):
If you see someone being followed, harassed, or cornered on the street, don’t look away. Move closer, create a distraction, ask them a neutral question (like "Do you know what time it is?"), or stay nearby until they are safe. Your presence can disrupt a crime.
2️⃣ Illuminate the Dark Spaces:
Work with local youth, community groups, and local leaders to identify poorly lit streets, quiet alleyways, and blind spots. Demand better lighting, and encourage shop owners and residents to keep their exterior lights on at night. A well-lit neighborhood is a safer neighborhood.
3️⃣ Establish Instant Check-Ins & Digital Escorts:
Never travel alone late at night without sharing your route. Utilize technology to your advantage. Setting up silent emergency triggers like SAFE bd (⁠safebd.onrender.com⁠) allows you to silently alert your family or dispatchers, broadcast your live GPS, and even preserve evidence without having to type or make a call during a panic.
4️⃣ Keep Every Number That Counts Close:
Educate your children, peers, and elderly neighbors on key national emergency contacts. Ensure these are saved on speed dial and taught in every household:
 📞 999 – National Emergency Service (Police, Fire, Ambulance)
 📞 109 – National Helpline for Violence Against Women and Children
 👥 Local Community Watch / Thana (Police Station)
5️⃣ Look Out for the Most Vulnerable:
Build a "buddy system" for kids walking home from school, workers returning late at night, and elderly residents. Knowing our neighbors’ routines means we notice when something is off.
Let's refuse to let fear dictate how we live. Reach out to your neighbor, keep your eyes open, and support one another. Together, we are an unbreakable shield.
📥 Share this post, take this image, and pass it on to your friends, family, and local groups to show we stand together!
